title: docs(qa): 18.0 sweep anchor round 18 — approvals.record-page-decisions re-derived against the shipped record page, the packaged-automation board's Activation cell and 22 own-port boot respellings
body:
Refs #24579
Clause-②: no

Round 18 of the 18.0 sweep's wave anchor (claim `6304655523`, PM loop round 33). It applies round 17's three carried checklist-text findings, PR #25003's out-of-scope findings as its ACCEPT `6304389370` and landing record `6304641541` carry them: `approvals.record-page-decisions` re-derived against the record page objectui ships, `automation.setup-packaged-automation-board` `steps[3]`, and 22 other texts that named the own-port boot or its DB "isolated".

Only checklist text changes. 19 items in 6 area files each take one `revision` bump and one `history` row, and each row names PR #25003 and its finding. There is no product code, test, pin, changeset text or `RUNNER.md` change, no new item, and every item id is kept.

- Base `93e6c1a5f8`. `origin/main` `62bc129308` is merged in `1fa304d42f`. Its one commit touches `packages/cli` only: no `docs/qa/**` path and none of the sources these edits cite.
- Every item was read at the base, and every objectui source at the console pin `cf153eb2e535` (`.objectui-sha` on `main`), with `git show` from a full scratch clone (`--is-shallow-repository` false). objectui `99782f961` (objectui#3055) is an ancestor of the pin: exit 0. Control, the pin as an ancestor of `99782f961`: exit 1.
- A scripted span editor made every edit. It is round 17's editor, unchanged (same sha256), and it never re-serialises a file. For each area file it re-parses the result and asserts four things, and all six files passed:
  - A1: the new document equals the old one with the declared ops applied.
  - A2: every other item and top-level key is value-equal.
  - A3: each edited item's changed paths lie inside its declared fields (array edits by exact index), plus `revision` and the one new history row.
  - A4: the text outside the edited items is byte-identical.
- A whole-branch check against the base agrees: 19 items changed, each with revision +1 and exactly one appended row, and no other file or path changed.
- The new history rows carry the placeholder ref `#PENDING-24579R18`, because a row's `ref` names this PR and the PR had no number yet. The next commit on this branch swaps in this PR's number and changes nothing else. The gates are re-run on that head, and the report comment on #24579 records them.
- The live verdicts at the pin are NOT MEASURED. The objectui and server sources were read, not run.

## 1. `approvals.record-page-decisions` (revision 3 → 4)

At `cf153eb2e535` the record page draws no header Approve/Reject. `RecordDetailView.tsx` (blob `64a7c675e50d`) mounts `DeclaredActionsBar` (blob `f27b4ab0efff`) above the page body whenever the record has a pending request. The dispatch record is the pending `sys_approval_request` row, the location is `record_section`, and `approval_remind` is excluded (`recordApprovalActions.ts`, blob `f6aabe078ea0`). The bar reads `sys_approval_request`'s declared actions and evaluates each one's `visible` predicate, failing closed, against the row's `viewer` block. The server computes that block per caller (`ApprovalService.attachViewers`: `can_act`, `is_submitter`, `can_override`). `useRecordApprovals.ts` (blob `b65a91f4a9a4`) only reads, and holds no `canDecide`.

The steps, numbered from 1 as the item's own text numbers them:

The bar shows Override Approve / Override Reject / Override Reassign (amber, `data-override-decision`), no Send back or Request info, and a plain Recall and Reply | `DeclaredActionsBar.tsx` and `approvalOverride.ts` (`isOverrideDecision`); the declarations' `can_override` arms |

The off-slate admin's Override framing is recorded separately | `ApprovalService.attachViewers` and `decide`; `request-read-gate.ts`; `DeclaredActionsBar.tsx` |

The item's other fields:

- `title`: "Approve/Reject render in the record header; …" → "Approve/Reject render on the record page from sys_approval_request's declared actions; …". The intent (deciding an approval from the record page), the id and the priority (P2) are kept.
- `fixtures.requires[0]` now says that exec_review is reached only after manager_review approves, and that the admin holds `exec` and submits each request. `fixtures.requires[1]`: `buildApprovalDecisionActions` → `DeclaredActionsBar` over the pending row, `recordApprovalActions.ts`, and the server's declarations.
- `fixtures.knownGaps[0]`, round 17's note about the retired text, is removed. It was the only entry, so `fixtures.knownGaps` goes.
- `negative[2]`: "Approve/Reject rendered on the header for a viewer who is not a pending approver (canDecide false)" → a declared decision action rendered for a viewer whose `viewer` block admits none.
- `source[0]` and `source[1]` now cite `RecordDetailView.tsx` and `DeclaredActionsBar.tsx` (with `useRecordApprovals.ts` and `useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx`) at the pin. `source[4]` (the declarations and `attachViewers`) and `source[5]` (the read gate and `decide`) are added. `source[2]` (the two pins) and `source[3]` (the flow) are unchanged.
- No `automated` is added. The item had no `automated` field at the base: round 17 re-pointed `source[2]`. Neither pin holds a clause whole at its layer. objectui's `RecordDetailView.approvalDeclaredActions.test.tsx` (blob `9519ae70f743`) mounts the page in jsdom over a fetch double, with a hand-written `sys_approval_request` definition and the param dialog mocked. `sys-approval-request.object.test.ts` reads the declarations.

## 2. `automation.setup-packaged-automation-board` `steps[3]` (revision 6 → 7)

Old: "confirm every switch reads On except a flow authored status: 'obsolete' (showcase_approver_bindings, …), whose switch correctly reads Off — 31 On / 1 Off at QA run #24545's subject".

New: the Activation cell is read as two facts. The switch shows the activation flag. The badge beside it (`data-testid` `packaged-flow-activation`, with a `data-reading` attribute) reads 'On' for an enabled flow whose `_status` row carries no `unboundCause`, 'Not running here' with the switch still checked for one that carries one, and 'Off' with the switch unchecked for a disabled flow. On a default boot `showcase_scheduled_digest` and `showcase_task_due_reminder` carry `deployment_policy`. Sources at the pin: `packagedFlows.ts` `activationReading` (blob `a85c96d28e5a`) and `PackagedAutomationPage.tsx` (blob `f4aa90e11d32`). At the base: `describeUnboundReason` (service-automation `engine.ts`), `FLOW_UNBOUND_CAUSES` (spec `automation-service.ts`) and RUNNER.md's scheduled-work entry.

The count is stated with its derivation from the 32 flows `allFlows` declares at `93e6c1a5f8` (`examples/app-showcase/src/automation/flows/index.ts`), each classified by its authored `status` and its start trigger:

| flows | count | reads on a default boot |
|:--|--:|:--|
| record-triggered (18) and `api`-triggered (1), all of which bind | 19 | On |
| no trigger: screen flows and invoked subflows | 10 | On |
| `type: 'schedule'`: `showcase_scheduled_digest` (interval), `showcase_task_due_reminder` (time_relative) | 2 | Not running here |
| `status: 'obsolete'`: `showcase_approver_bindings` | 1 | Off |

That is 29 On / 2 Not running here / 1 Off, and 31 On / 1 Off with `OS_AUTOMATION_SCHEDULED_WORK_ENABLED` exported. The 19 that bind agree with RUNNER.md's measured banner, `32 flow(s) 19 bound` on a default boot and `21 bound` with the switch. Only `obsolete` and `invalid` disable a flow (`flowStatusDisabled` in the engine), so the 10 flows with no authored `status` (`draft`) are enabled. The step tells the run to reconcile against `_status` rather than these digits.

- 41 name the `isolated` tenancy posture (`OS_TENANCY_POSTURE=isolated`, "group/isolated", walled boots). They are untouched. One of them sits in an edited item: `access-security.platform-owner-email-anchor` `steps[0]`, "a walled posture (group / isolated)".
- 2 are other senses and are untouched: "Saved reports are owner-isolated" (`dashboards.saved-report-ownership`, its title) and "unroutable from the isolated env" (`automation.flow-error-handling`).

## Acceptance notes

- Some edits sit beyond the dispatch's field list, inside the item it names, to keep that item consistent with its own re-derivation: `title` (it said "render in the record header"), `fixtures.requires[0]` (exec_review is reached only after manager_review approves), `negative[2]` (it named `canDecide`), the new `steps[9]`, and `source[4]`–`[5]`.
- The dispatch says to keep `automated.ref` only for clauses a pin asserts whole at their layer. The item carries no `automated` at the base, because round 17 re-pointed `source[2]`, and neither pin holds a clause whole at its layer. So none is added.
- `acceptance[4]`'s oracle moves from `dom` to `api`. The clause is the server's gate, and RUNNER.md rule 4 makes the server the authority. The UI absence is still read, after a screenshot.
- On a stock showcase the closed-side member reads no request at all. The approvals door serves requests to participants and to the override actor, and the record-reader tier is off. So the member's page draws no bar, rather than a bar with every button hidden, and the forged POST is the server-side proof.
- The off-slate admin also keeps a plain Recall and Reply, because the admin submitted the request. `isOverrideDecision` leaves a lever the viewer holds through its submitter arm unframed (objectui#13225).

## Gates

The derived list is `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`. It is computed on the actual change set: 6 paths against merge base `62bc12930`, at head `1fa304d42f`. It gives 13 commands. Each one ran at that head with its exit code captured before any pipe, and each exited 0:

`node scripts/check-ci-filter-parity.mjs` · `node scripts/check-closing-keyword-parity.mjs` · `node scripts/check-closing-keyword-parity.mjs --self-test` · `node scripts/check-comment-mask-corpus.mjs` · `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint run check:doc-formula-expressions` · `pnpm check:cross-package-test-inputs` · `pnpm check:doc-authoring` · `pnpm check:driver-memory-census` · `pnpm check:gitlink-declared` · `pnpm check:nul-bytes` · `pnpm check:platform-checklist` · `pnpm check:refd-timer-probe` · `pnpm check:watch-hint-literal`

The same 13 were run before the merge, at `46f612b0a1`. There, the first run of `check:doc-formula-expressions` refused with exit 3, a prerequisite: `@objectstack/formula` and `@objectstack/lint` were not built. Both were built under the shared verify lock (`VERDICT command-exit 0`, held 11 s, waited 0 s), and the rerun exited 0. The `--ran` reconciliation reads "13 derived, 13 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN" at both heads.

No per-PR CI job runs `pnpm check:platform-checklist`, so this local reading is its evidence:

| items | 16 areas, 328 items (323 active, 1 planned) | 16 areas, 328 items (323 active, 1 planned) |

| symbol anchors | 975/985 against 433 cited sources, 10 on the named residual (#16898), 18 file floors held | 979/989 against 434 cited sources, 10 on the named residual (#16898), 18 file floors held |

The four new anchors all resolve: `seed-approval-demo.ts#ADMIN_APPROVAL_POSITIONS`, `sys-approval-request.object.ts#approval_reject`, `approval-service.ts#attachViewers` and `approval-service.ts#decide`. No line citation is added.

`git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` exited 0 against `62bc129308`. No open PR touches `docs/qa/platform-checklist/`: all 16 open PRs' file lists were read over REST, and the three with more than 100 files were read page by page, at 349, 367 and 235 files, each equal to its `changed_files`. So there was no second merge-tree to run.

There is no ablation, because no tested behaviour changed. `skip-changeset` was re-measured: no `files[]` entry of the 73 non-private manifests (86 tracked `package.json` files) reaches outside its own package or names `docs/qa`, and the repo root is private.
